kind: coding agent with remote plan service

runtime.execution: Go CLI/TUI consumes Go HTTP plan server; Go goroutines stream planner/summary/per-file build requests; client applies staged changes and launches local shell process groups. Server starts LiteLLM proxy.
runtime.service_boundary: Client owns local file application/command process; server owns plan jobs, Git plan repositories/active stream state and its proxy, consumes PostgreSQL/model endpoints. It is a plan service consumer/owner split, not arbitrary shared kernel fabric.

summary: Remote staged-plan coding agent with model role pipeline, context maps/loading, cumulative file changes, operator-selectable automation and failure-driven local execution/retry.

inspection.scope: Selected source excerpts trace exposed entry/loop/request/action/result/state boundaries and relevant capability mechanisms; listed tests are read as source only.
inspection.limits: No acquired code executed, dependencies installed or live providers invoked. Claims concern this pinned snapshot; untraced catalog tools and dependency internals are not inferred.

actions.name: tell / POST /plans/{planId}/{branch}/tell
actions.input: Prompt or piped/file text; branch, context/build/auto-continue/exec flags, session ID
actions.output: Streaming reply/build/load events, model-stream ID, staged plan state or errors
actions.lifecycle: Launches server job; --bg returns while server continues; same plan/branch active stream rejected
actions.authority: Operator/program auth and plan authorization; model participates through response protocol

actions.name: PlandexBlock / ### Move Files / ### Remove Files / ### Reset Changes
actions.input: File path/lang/content; source/destination or paths; end tags
actions.output: Operation records and per-path pending builds/staged file results
actions.lifecycle: Parsed from streamed text; queues build work while planning may continue
actions.authority: Model emits operations; server dispatch enabled outside chat-only and according to build mode; local apply separate

actions.name: ### Files → AutoLoadContextFiles / POST .../auto_load_context
actions.input: Backtick file paths restricted to submitted project map; client uploads selected file bodies
actions.output: Context records, skip/size messages and acknowledgement for server wait
actions.lifecycle: UI performs local reads; server waits 30 seconds then continues/errors
actions.authority: Model selects within available paths; authenticated client has filesystem access and bounds

actions.name: build / PATCH /plans/{planId}/{branch}/build
actions.input: Pending proposed operations grouped by path
actions.output: PlanFileResult staged content/removal and build events/IDs
actions.lifecycle: Go workers concurrent across paths; per-path queue and flags
actions.authority: Server model roles generate/apply structured proposal; no workspace execution implied by build

actions.name: apply / PATCH /plans/{planId}/{branch}/apply
actions.surface: operator command / local client + server API
actions.output: Local file changes, optional project commit, server applied state, rollback record
actions.lifecycle: Tentatively writes files, then command execution; success commits server applied state
actions.authority: Operator manual or selected full-auto flags; proposed model content interpreted by client

actions.name: _apply.sh / execApplyScript
actions.input: Shell script or explicit command; inherited cwd/env/stdin
actions.output: Live merged output, exit code, success/failure; no durable process handle
actions.lifecycle: Local process group; forwarded signal then 2-second kill escalation; temp script removed
actions.authority: AutoExec or operator confirmation; ordinary OS authority; generated set/trap/shebang lines rewritten

actions.name: GetOnApplyExecFail / debug retry
actions.input: Exit status/output, rollback plan, attempt bound
actions.output: New failure prompt, planner changes and next application attempt
actions.lifecycle: Rollback tracked file changes then TellPlan/apply; configured attempt limit may prompt user for extension
actions.authority: Operator chooses autonomy; model fixes project task through ordinary plan loop, not harness refit protocol

actions.name: continue
actions.input: Current plan/branch and refreshed config-derived flags
actions.output: New streamed planner iteration on persisted plan state
actions.lifecycle: New request with IsUserContinue; active stream exclusion applies
actions.authority: Authenticated operator; no serialized suspended provider request

actions.name: connect / PATCH .../connect / ps
actions.output: Existing server stream rendered in new client
actions.lifecycle: Attach to still-running server; not a new provider peer
actions.authority: Authorized operator; server work outlives detached client

actions.name: stop / DELETE .../stop
actions.output: Abort event, stopped partial message when persistence succeeds
actions.lifecycle: Routes to owning host; cancellation deferred even if partial-store operation fails
actions.authority: Authenticated plan authority; stop cancels plan and summary, local command needs separate OS signal

actions.name: convo / log / GET .../convo / GET .../logs
actions.input: Plan/branch; client conversation or Git history selection
actions.output: Original stored conversation JSON or Git log/SHA list
actions.lifecycle: Read repository operation; corrupt message read errors; log retention/history scope differs
actions.authority: Authenticated operator; no full-event model query language traced

actions.name: rewind / PATCH .../rewind
actions.input: Target SHA; optional local project reversion choice
actions.output: Reset plan repository and token metadata, optional local restored files
actions.lifecycle: Git hard-reset state rollback; further local restoration can fail independently
actions.authority: Authenticated operator; not model projection repair preserving immutable event history

actions.name: set-config / set-auto / PUT /plans/{planId}/config
actions.output: Stored config; command cache updated by client paths
actions.lifecycle: Config write immediate; CLI captures flags at command boundary; server reloads role settings each iteration
actions.authority: Operator/config API; no model editable workflow language or deferred affected-work fence exposed

actions.name: RegisterHook / ExecHook
actions.input: Hook name and Go function; structured plan/auth/request/build payloads
actions.lifecycle: Synchronous registration/execution; some dispatchers call asynchronously
actions.authority: Server program/deployment code; not normal model-discovered user script

actions.name: RegisterNotifyErrFn / NotifyErr
actions.lifecycle: No registered callback means no-op; callback panics caught
actions.authority: Host/server integration; no state-rich model bead contract

filesystem.detail: Model text proposes file/move/remove/reset operations; server stages results, client loads files and later applies local writes with rollback metadata. Application is not a transactional filesystem sandbox.

processes.detail: Client runs generated _apply.sh with inherited OS authority/process group, merged output and signal escalation. Server also owns a LiteLLM proxy. No persistent shell job handle traced.

code_actions.detail: Model-produced _apply.sh composes OS commands and is executed by local client; streamed file operations/builds produce code edits rather than model-authored programs composing harness tools. No general tool-code interpreter traced.

persistent_kernel.detail: Inspected planner/build loop and local _apply.sh execution establish fresh command processes; persistent evaluable kernel/session variables are not established.

standing_database.detail: Server consumes PostgreSQL for plan/config/summary metadata with timeouts; no model-accessible standing SQL/data-workspace action was traced.

workflow_programming.detail: Fixed context→planning→implementation/build/apply/debug workflow with model-produced task/operation text and tunable automation. Server Go hooks permit embedding; no ordinary model-editable orchestration program/discovery was traced.

multi_model.detail: Architect/planner/coder/builder/summary roles resolve actual model requests and role packs; per-file builders and background summary can overlap. This is pipeline role division, not peer room.

live_collaboration.detail: Remote plan streams permit operator reconnection and multiple model roles. Same plan/branch rejects concurrent active streams; inspected paths expose no live model peer mailbox/room.

concurrent_work.detail: Server Go planner jobs, background summaries, per-file build queues and independent plans/branches overlap; process-local active registry plus DB host metadata coordinate streams. Ordering/race invariants not runtime-validated.

steering_interrupt.detail: Stop delivers abort then partial-save attempt and cancellation; CLI commands can restart/continue against saved state. Local shell signal handling is separate from remote plan stop. No busy-turn prompt injection traced.

turn_redefinition.detail: Model creates/removes task/operation text and configured AutoContinue governs a compiled stage machine. Go hooks can gate requests; no general model-authorized redefinition of turn program exposed.

compaction.detail: Summary rows separate from original per-message JSON; budget selects fitting summary prefix then later original messages. Timestamp-based projection and ID fallback are actual mechanisms, not loss validation.

context_repair.detail: Original conversations and Git plan rewind/reload support operator reconstruction; model can request additional mapped file context. No model-issued summary repair/restoration with original-event attribution protocol traced; rewind resets plan history head.

original_audit.detail: Original conversation/state files and Git commits are retained separately from summary projection, but debug logs rotate, request dump is commented out, optional request-completion hooks may be absent/fail, shell captures scanner text only. Not comprehensive immutable audit.

audit_query.detail: Authenticated conversation and Git history/SHA APIs permit useful plan study; internal SQL summary query exists. No unified query over provider wire/process/UI/config/original event stream traced.

hot_change.detail: Operator config updates persist immediately; CLI resolves automation flags at command start while server role/org settings reload each planner iteration. No coherent fence after all affected workflows or apply-now operation established.

rebuild_continuity.detail: Detached client can reconnect to a living server; new continue request reconstructs plan state. Server shutdown waits bounded time before HTTP shutdown/proxy cleanup. No executable-context outpost handoff or enforced request/program quiescence before refit.

remote_services.detail: CLI consumes authenticated cloud/self-host Go plan service and SSE streams; server consumes model HTTP services/DB and starts its own LiteLLM proxy. This server governs plan jobs rather than treating all computation as external shared fabric.

self_improvement.detail: Bounded automated failure→rollback→model fix→apply cycle can improve arbitrary project work; no model-governed harness autoresearch criterion/experiment selection/recompile continuity protocol traced.

complaints.detail: RegisterNotifyErrFn provides host-injected error monitoring; absent callback no-ops. No model-invocable grievance filing that captures agent state/database bead semantics traced.

authority.detail: Server APIs authenticate and authorize plans; autonomy presets can bypass routine apply/command confirmation. Local command inherits environment/stdin and OS authority; model is constrained by compiled response protocol and operator-supplied execution flags.

evaluation.detail: Read fixture oracles for exact operation rendering/state, task extraction and unique replacement. Stream processor test omits shouldStop assertion; none of these establishes provider/process cancellation, plan concurrency, summary fidelity or refit conformance. Not run.

time_order.detail: Creation timestamps order conversations/summaries; stream/build/plan IDs identify work. Actual first-token/inactivity, file-load and command signal/shutdown deadlines differ. No unified causal event order/audit time semantics established.

evidence.claim: Go HTTP server starts/owns a LiteLLM proxy, registers proxy shutdown, initializes DB and serves routes.
CLI resolves project/auth and config-derived flags, calls TellPlan, optionally applies local changes after it returns.
CLI submits prompt, project path set, execution/context/build/continuation flags and session ID to remote TellPlan.
Authenticated authorized TellPlan handler decodes request, initializes provider clients, launches modelPlan.Tell and optionally connects response stream.
Tell activates plan and launches an asynchronous Go planner iteration; return means launched, not completed.
Activation rejects existing in-memory or DB model streams for plan/branch and records host and model-stream identity.
Context/planning/implementation stages select architect/planner/coder role configurations.
Request selects fallback, builds streamed messages/config/stop token, retains original request in RAM, starts provider call and listener; request-file dump is commented out.
Provider request JSON posts to configured chat-completions URL with context, auth and SSE stream reader; actual HTTP request dispatch is wired.
Separate goroutine receives blocking stream chunks while main listener handles context cancellation and first-token/inactivity timeout; retry allowed before any content.
Chunks feed ReplyParser, optionally use visible reasoning, guard an existing-but-unloaded file, append rendered reply, stream it and dispatch new operations.
Parser recognizes file-labelled/XML PlandexBlock and move/remove/reset section headers; completed code block becomes file operation.
Remove/reset paths become deduplicated pending operations; parser exposes file/operation state and tokens.
New operations queue build work in auto build mode with reply/path/content/move/remove/reset fields and append active operation list.
Go build queues are grouped by path with IsBuildingByPath flags; different paths launch asynchronous builds while same-path work is queued.
Move queues separate remove/create builds; removal returns a staged PlanFileResult rather than mutating operator workspace.
New files yield staged content result; existing files dispatch structured edit strategy.
Whole-file fallback prepares source/proposal prompt, selects builder role and invokes model.ModelRequest with plan/build/message identities.
Finished reply is stored before launching background summary model call using separately cancellable SummaryCtx.
File load requests stream to client, wait up to 30 seconds for client acknowledgement, then continuation launches a new planner iteration.
Planning stage follows context/task flags and AutoContinue; implementation checks task completion and 200-iteration cap. That cap is not applied to planning branch.
Model selects backtick-enclosed file paths from declared ProjectPaths during planning; ### Files counts explicit selection.
Client loads selected files with file/count/total-size limits, encodes images/normalizes text, and calls AutoLoadContext even for empty selection to release waiting server.
TUI response dispatcher starts loadContextCmd for server load request and quits on error/finish/abort.
loadContextCmd calls real AutoLoadContextFiles with its own background-derived cancellation context; completion is UI message.
Local tentative ApplyFiles precedes execution; success then marks server plan applied and optionally commits operator project.
_apply.sh or explicit command content is shown and executed only after user confirmation or AutoExec.
Generated script gets fixed shell error header, removes user shebang/set/trap lines, writes local executable script and starts shell with inherited environment/stdin and merged stdout/stderr.
Signal handler forwards signals to group then SIGKILL after 2 seconds; waits command, collects scanner text, asks success after interrupt and feeds exit/output into failure continuation.
Local command uses process group and negative PID signal targeting.
AutoDebug compares attempt bound, otherwise offers operator choices; retry rolls back tracked file changes, sends failure status/output to TellPlan and reapplies recursively.
Conversation budget selects stored summary that fits limits; timestamp lookup has message-ID fallback, and missing usable summary can error.
Request projection retains stored conversation separately: summary replaces prefix for provider request, later messages selected by timestamp; no summary deletion of originals here.
Summaries are separate PostgreSQL rows filtered by latest conversation message ID and ordered by created_at.
Original conversation messages are per-ID JSON files; retrieval fails on unreadable/corrupt files, sorts by creation time; store writes file and DB token metadata.
Authenticated APIs expose Git history/SHA list and plan rewind; rewind resets repository and synchronizes token metadata.
Plan rewind calls git reset --hard to requested SHA; it is ordinary Git state rollback, not immutable original event retention.
After server rewind, client can optionally apply analyzed project changes to local workspace, separately confirmed.
Stop routes to active host, authenticates/authorizes, sends aborted message, attempts partial-reply persistence and defers cancel even if DB operation fails.
Stop cancels summary and active plan; stopped partial assistant message is saved through StoreConvoMessage.
Every planner iteration reloads settings and org-user configuration under repository operation; request flags remain supplied request state.
Operator execution flags derive from plan config at CLI command start unless explicitly supplied.
Authorized config update writes config immediately; handler does not enqueue activation fence or cancel an active plan.
Server program may register in-process hook function; no-hook execution succeeds with empty result. This is compiled embedding API, not discovered model script interface.
Optional completion hook receives request/result and model/plan/message IDs asynchronously; hook error only logged.
Client debug logger rotates at 10 MB with 3 backups and 28-day age; debug log is not unlimited audit retention.
Shutdown waits up to 60 seconds for active plans before HTTP shutdown and registered hooks; request admission is not closed before wait in this path.
Client consumes cloud/default or authenticated self-host server with auth/version headers.
Server consumes configured PostgreSQL DB with timeout settings and connection pool; it is internal plan storage rather than model standing SQL interface.
Full-auto preset enables continuation/build/context/apply/commit/exec/debug and five auto debug attempts.
Server embedding may register monitoring callback; unregistered NotifyErr is no-op. No exposed model complaint action/state bead traced.
CLI reconnects chosen plan/branch to existing server stream and starts terminal UI.
Continue launches a new TellPlan request with IsUserContinue rather than resuming a serialized in-flight stack.
Native APIs expose current state, apply, rejection, diffs, context CRUD/body, conversation, rewind, logs, branches, settings, status and tell/build.
Native API routing exposes model packs/config/active-stream connection/stop/missing-file/auto-context acknowledgement.
Table tests compare buffer/render/parser-state fields but do not assert got.shouldStop despite stop cases; isolated parser tests not provider/process lifecycle.
Replacement fixtures check exact unique/no/ambiguous-match return strings.
Task parser asserts length and exact title/description/uses-files values against fixtures.
ApplyFiles gathers rollback content/mode before local writes, excludes _apply.sh, writes multiple files via Go goroutines.
Operator set-config/set-auto commands retrieve, mutate and submit plan configuration.
Default role pack assigns architect/planner/coder, summary, builder, namer/commit/status roles across model configurations.
Server starts Python uvicorn litellm_proxy subprocess with stdout/stderr forwarding; confirms supporting runtime role and ownership.

tests.focus: Partial tag/stop-prefix rendering and parser state transitions
tests.oracle: Table expected stream/content/buffer/state comparisons; shouldStop is present in fixtures but not compared. Pure helper tests, not a provider/command lifecycle oracle.
Exact expected matched string or empty rejection for fixed fixtures, no generative/file lifecycle evidence.
Exact fixture count/title/description/file-list assertions; no planner semantic correctness.

strengths: Separates proposed edits from local application and traces failure-driven rollback/retry with explicit autonomy levels.
Persisted conversation originals plus separate summary projections and plan Git versions allow useful context/history study.
Go service/client separation exposes durable plan/branch/stream identity, client reconnect and concurrent per-file construction.
limits: Fixed response-text protocol/stage machine is much narrower than general model-editable workflow/turn programs.
Stop preserves partial reply best effort and cancels; local command cancellation separate; no outpost/refit quiescence protocol.
Conversation/state/version retention and optional request hook are not a full immutable core audit.
Implementation continuation has 200 cap but inspected planning branch does not apply it.
Read parser tests omit shouldStop assertion; lifecycle/concurrency/summary loss remain unvalidated.
Go/native service architecture is study material and does not override operator language distrust or imply adoption.
arconaut_questions: Can staged-plan changes be a programmable workflow option while preserving ordinary direct-tool modes and model control over programs?
Which work identity belongs to Arconaut client versus separately governed fabric, and what continues across client refit without pausing shared service?
How should original conversation/event storage support model repair of a selected summary projection without a destructive whole-plan rewind?
How should configuration versions bind to complete affected workflows when role settings refresh every iteration but command flags were captured earlier?
What direct cancellation/quiescence oracle detects remaining provider receivers, local process groups and background summaries before arcorefit?
Should failure diagnosis retain raw command bytes and uncertain effects rather than reconstruct only scanner text and rollback known file edits?
